title: Retroperitoneal Ectopic Bronchogenic Cyst Mimicking an Adrenal Mass: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND Bronchogenic cysts (BCs) are rare congenital anomalies that are extremely uncommon in the retroperitoneum; in this uncommon anatomical location, they are frequently misdiagnosed radiologically as solid adrenal or pancreatic tumors. This report aims to enhance clinical awareness and diagnostic vigilance regarding ectopic retroperitoneal bronchogenic cysts (ERBCs) that closely mimic other common endocrine or urological entities. CASE REPORT We report a case of a middle-aged man presenting with recurrent right flank pain. Abdominal computed tomography (CT) demonstrated multiple right renal calculi with mild hydronephrosis and a well-defined, homogeneous nodular lesion in the right adrenal region. Notably, the lesion exhibited a high unenhanced density (mean 48.79 HU), mimicking a solid adrenal neoplasm. Following comprehensive hormonal and biochemical evaluations, a multidisciplinary team determined that a retroperitoneal tumor could not be ruled out. The patient subsequently underwent laparoscopic resection of the retroperitoneal mass combined with right ureteral stent placement. Intraoperative exploration revealed a morphologically regular adrenal gland and a separate 4×2.5×1.5 cm oval mass located on the psoas major muscle. Histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of a benign bronchogenic cyst, characterized by a cyst wall containing prominent cartilaginous components, smooth muscle, and a lining of pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium. The patient recovered uneventfully, with complete symptom resolution. CONCLUSIONS ERBCs should be included in the differential diagnosis of non-functional lesions in the periadrenal region, especially when atypical high CT attenuation creates diagnostic ambiguity. Minimally invasive laparoscopic excision remains the gold standard for management.

title: CT-RSA with induced displacement used for assessment of aseptic loosening of distal femur reconstructions with megaprostheses in patients reporting pain.
abstract: Aims The aim of this study was to evaluate the relationship between experienced pain and findings of suspected pathological movement on CT-radiostereometric analysis (RSA) with induced displacement. Methods Patients with reported pain after distal femur reconstruction with a megaprosthesis between January 2000 and December 2022 indicated the pain they experienced at rest and during activity using a visual analogue scale (VAS) and a pain drawing. Two consecutive CT scans with induced displacement were performed for each patient. The translational and rotational movement between bone and implant in the tibia and femur were calculated and compared with reported pain location and type at rest and during activity. Results A total of 12 patients were examined; ten had measured movement above the preset cutoff values for pathological movement in either femur, tibia, or both. A large inter-patient variability in translation and rotation was found. The movements for the femur components were up to 3.46 mm/1.14° (translation/rotation). For the tibia components, these values were 2.16 mm/2.95°. Overall, six of 12 patients reported a severe type of pain. All six had a suspected loose implant at the location marked on their pain drawing. Six of 12 patients had a > 30 mm difference on VAS between rest and activity; five of those six had a suspected loose implant according to CT-RSA. Conclusion CT-RSA with induced displacement appears useful for diagnosing suspected pathological movements in megaprosthesis implants. Pain locations on drawings seem to match detected suspected loose implants. Further studies with repeated CT-RSA examinations are needed to establish reliable cutoff values and assist decisions on revision surgery.

title: Causes of Death Among Stillbirths and Children Aged <5 Years in Africa and South Asia - Child Health and Mortality Prevention Surveillance, Seven Countries, 2016-2024.
abstract: Problem/condition Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia have the highest rates of stillbirths and rates of death among children aged <5 years, with many countries in those regions unlikely to meet the 2030 goal of ending preventable deaths among newborns and children aged <5 years. Conventional mortality surveillance (determining cause of death through interviews with family members or caregivers [i.e., verbal autopsy] and vital registration) in areas with high mortality often lacks laboratory confirmation of causes and incompletely identifies maternal contributors and comorbid conditions, providing information that is insufficiently specific to guide prevention efforts. Period covered December 2016-December 2024. Description of system The Child Health and Mortality Prevention Surveillance (CHAMPS) network generates standardized, laboratory-confirmed data on causes and preventability of deaths among neonates, infants, and children aged <5 years and stillbirths in areas with high mortality. During 2016-2024, CHAMPS operated in seven countries (Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Kenya, Mali, Mozambique, Sierra Leone, and South Africa) through population-defined catchment areas. Eligibility required residence in a CHAMPS catchment area for ≥4 months before death or, for children aged <4 months, since birth. Deaths were investigated using a standardized postmortem approach that included minimally invasive tissue sampling (MITS), laboratory investigations (conventional and molecular microbiology and histopathology), interviews with family members or caregivers (i.e., verbal autopsy), and pediatric and maternal clinical record abstraction. Multidisciplinary determination of cause-of-death (DeCoDe) panels integrated evidence to assign causes (including multiple causes per death) and assess preventability. Results During 2016-2024, a total of 18,784 eligible deaths were identified; families consented to CHAMPS enrollment for 15,612 (83.1%) of these deaths. MITS was completed for 9,415 deaths and DeCoDe was completed for 8,500 (90.3% of MITS-investigated deaths); a total of 3,199 (37.6%) were stillbirths; 3,230 (38.0%) were neonatal deaths; and 2,071 (24.4%) were deaths of infants (aged 28 days to <12 months) and children (aged ≥12 to <60 months). Stillbirths were predominantly attributed to perinatal asphyxia or hypoxia (79.1%), often with maternal hypertensive disorders, placental abnormalities, chorioamnionitis, and other medical conditions (e.g., diabetes). Neonatal deaths involved preterm complications (39.7%); asphyxia or hypoxia (37.7%), which often is linked to maternal and intrapartum care; and sepsis (36.5%), commonly resulting from infection with Klebsiella pneumoniae and Acinetobacter baumannii. Among infants and children, leading causes of death included lower respiratory infections (37.4%), sepsis (36.9%), malnutrition (27.3%), malaria (22.1%), and diarrheal disease (17.3%). Multiple conditions in the causal chain were common among neonates (44.3% with two or more conditions) and infants and children (67.9% with two or more conditions). Postmortem anthropometry indicated high levels of moderate or severe undernutrition among infants and children; among those with available measurements, nonmutually exclusive anthropometric indicators included underweight (61.3%), wasting (61.3%), and stunting (43.0%), according to the World Health Organization's Child Growth Standards. Among neonatal, infant, and child deaths (excluding stillbirths), infection contributed to 3,146 (59.3%) deaths. Among neonatal, infant, and child deaths with one or more pathogens identified in the causal chain (n = 2,749), 44.5% were polymicrobial, with gram-negative bacteria predominating. Main maternal conditions, most commonly placental complications and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, were assigned for 71.1% of stillbirths and 58.2% of neonatal deaths. Of 7,558 deaths with a preventability assessment, 6,103 (80.7%) were considered preventable or possibly preventable through improvements in already available maternal, newborn, and child health interventions; primary opportunities included strengthened antenatal care, obstetric management, and infection control. Interpretation CHAMPS complements conventional mortality surveillance by providing standardized, laboratory-confirmed, postmortem evidence on causes and preventability of stillbirths and of deaths among neonates, infants, and children aged <5 years across areas with high mortality. Findings demonstrate that preventable infections, suboptimal antenatal care, intrapartum complications, preterm birth, and malnutrition account for most deaths and also involve maternal and health care system factors. The predominance of infections caused by gram-negative bacteria highlights the need to strengthen infection prevention and control and to develop preventive tools, including vaccines. Public health action Four of every five deaths were potentially preventable with timely implementation of established maternal, newborn, and child health interventions. CHAMPS demonstrates that high-precision postmortem MITS is feasible in resource-constrained settings and provides data critical to improve maternal and child health planning, practice, and policy. Certain components of CHAMPS (e.g., standardized MITS training, targeted diagnostics, and multidisciplinary review) could be adapted to strengthen routine surveillance and mortality review systems where feasible.

title: When Thyrotropin Meets Growth Hormone: Clinical Challenges of a Mixed GH/TSH-Secreting PIT1-Lineage Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor
abstract: Background: Acromegaly is most commonly caused by a growth hormone (GH)-secreting pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET). Plurihormonal PIT1-lineage PitNETs are uncommon, and combined GH and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) secretion poses distinctive diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We report a mixed GH/TSH-secreting PIT1-lineage PitNET in which biochemical response to preoperative lanreotide supported the clinical suspicion of co-secretion before histopathological confirmation. Case Presentation: A 39-year-old woman presented with a two-year history of progressive acral enlargement, headaches, hyperhidrosis, snoring, and voice deepening. Biochemical evaluation showed IGF-1 1128 ng/mL (reference range 93.1–281), GH 61 µg/L, TSH 1.5 µIU/mL (0.35–4.94), FT4 1.66 ng/dL (0.7–1.5), and FT3 7.0 pg/mL (1.8–4.2). Pituitary MRI demonstrated a 15 × 14 × 10.5 mm macroadenoma. Lanreotide 120 mg every four weeks reduced IGF-1 to 846 ng/mL and GH to 14 µg/L, while normalizing FT4 (1.04 ng/dL) and FT3 (3.9 pg/mL), reinforcing suspicion of mixed GH/TSH secretion. Transsphenoidal surgery was performed in October 2024. The tumor was initially classified as a densely granulated somatotroph PitNET; prompted by the preoperative biochemical phenotype, additional β-TSH immunostaining demonstrated positivity in numerous tumor cells, leading to reclassification as a mature plurihormonal PIT1-lineage PitNET (Ki-67 approximately 1%). Postoperative biochemical remission was not achieved, and MRI demonstrated a 7 mm residual lesion. Lanreotide was resumed, with sustained control of the thyrotroph component but persistent GH/IGF-1 excess. Because residual disease persisted with slight cavernous sinus extension, Gamma Knife radiosurgery was performed in July 2026. Conclusions: Mixed GH/TSH-secreting PIT1-lineage PitNETs may be overlooked when TSH is inappropriately normal rather than frankly elevated. This case illustrates the value of integrating biochemical findings, treatment response, and targeted histopathological reassessment. Persistent disease despite surgery and somatostatin receptor ligand therapy further highlights the frequent need for multimodal, long-term management.

title: Intraoperative recognition of low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm masquerading as a right ovarian tumor: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm (LAMN) is a mucin-producing epithelial tumor arising from the appendix. When the appendix is displaced into the pelvis and becomes cystically enlarged, LAMN may mimic a right ovarian mucinous tumor. Because rupture of LAMN may cause mucin spillage and pseudomyxoma peritonei, accurate intraoperative recognition and careful surgical handling are important. Case presentation: A 75-year-old Japanese woman was referred to our department with a right adnexal mass suspected to be an ovarian tumor. Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging revealed an approximately 7-cm cystic mass in the right adnexal region, and a right ovarian mucinous tumor was suspected preoperatively. Serum carcinoembryonic antigen was mildly elevated, whereas carbohydrate antigen 19 − 9 and cancer antigen 125 were not markedly elevated. Laparoscopic surgery was performed under the preoperative diagnosis of a right ovarian tumor. Intraoperatively, the uterus and bilateral adnexa were grossly normal. Instead, a cystic mass was identified near the right adnexal region and was continuous with the appendix and ileocecal region. The lesion was carefully resected without intraoperative rupture or mucin spillage. Intraoperative frozen section analysis showed no evidence of malignancy, and ascites cytology was negative. Histopathological examination revealed LAMN with a negative surgical margin. Immunohistochemical findings were consistent with an appendiceal origin and supported the diagnosis of LAMN. Postoperative computed tomography showed no evidence of residual disease or pseudomyxoma peritonei. Conclusion LAMN can mimic a right ovarian tumor. In right-sided mucinous adnexal masses, appendiceal origin should be considered, and rupture-free complete resection is essential to prevent pseudomyxoma peritonei.

title: BioPretext: A Multimodal Self-Supervised Learning Framework for Orthopedic Feature Extraction via Cross-Modal Signal Alignment and Dynamic Fusion
abstract: Abstract We propose BioPretext, a multimodal self-supervised learning (SSL) framework that unifies geometric and non-geometric biological signals for orthopedic feature extraction. Unlike conventional approaches that process imaging data independently, BioPretext exploits interactions between structural and functional modalities through cross-modal pretext tasks. The framework employs a dual-branch transformer architecture, where a vision transformer encodes geometric data (e.g., radiographs) and a temporal transformer processes sequential biological signals (e.g., EKG). Both representations are projected into a shared latent space via cross-attention. To improve robustness, two contrastive pretext tasks—signal inversion and time-window masking—are introduced, enabling recovery of corrupted or missing biological signals using geometric context. Extracted features are then integrated through a gated attention mechanism that adaptively weights modality contributions according to task relevance. The framework can replace conventional feature extraction modules in orthopedic AI systems and be readily applied to downstream tasks such as joint kinematics prediction and lesion segmentation. Key innovations include cross-modal SSL optimization, temporal-spatial alignment, and patient-specific dynamic fusion. Implemented with Swin Transformer and Performer backbones, BioPretext is pretrained on unlabeled multimodal datasets and subsequently fine-tuned for orthopedic applications. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance over unimodal SSL approaches, particularly in tasks involving complex interactions between biological and structural data, such as gait analysis and osteoarthritis grading. These findings highlight the potential of BioPretext as a scalable and generalizable framework for multimodal representation learning in orthopedics.

title: Qualitative MRI-Based Assessment of Hydrogel Spacer Distribution Predicts Rectal Dosimetry and Acute Toxicity in Prostate Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy
abstract: Abstract Background Hydrogel Rectal Spacers (HRS) are increasingly used to reduce rectal irradiation during stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) for localized prostate cancer (PCa). However, the clinical relevance of qualitative spacer distribution remains incompletely defined. This study evaluated whether MRI-based qualitative characteristics of HRS placement correlate with rectal dosimetry and acute rectal adverse events. Methods This prospective observational study included patients with localized PCa treated with transperineal HRS implantation followed by prostate SBRT between 2023 and 2025. Post-implant T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was used to assess spacer distribution according to three qualitative metrics: Spacer Quality Score (SQS), Symmetry Score (SYM), and Rectal Wall Infiltration score (RWI). Associations between spacer characteristics, rectal dosimetric parameters, and acute rectal toxicity, defined as events occurring within 6 months after SBRT, were analyzed. Results Seventy-six patients were included. Median prostate-rectum separation at the mid-gland level was 10 mm (range, 4–20 mm). SQS was significantly associated with rectal Dmax (p = 0.003), D1cc (p = 0.003), V36Gy (p = 0.018), V30Gy (p = 0.002), and V18Gy (p = 0.002). SYM score correlated with rectal V40Gy (p = 0.009). Acute rectal toxicity occurred in 18 patients (23.7%) and was significantly associated with SQS (p = 0.004). Rectal wall infiltration was identified in 20 patients (26.3%), including edema in 2 (2.6%) and superficial infiltration in 18 (23.7%), but did not correlate with acute rectal adverse events (p = 0.672). Conclusions MRI-based qualitative assessment of HRS distribution provides clinically meaningful information beyond spacer thickness alone. Optimal spacer distribution and symmetry were associated with improved rectal sparing and reduced acute rectal toxicity in patients undergoing prostate SBRT.

title: Computed Tomography Outcomes After Frozen Elephant Trunk for Type A Dissection: Single-Branched Versus Straight Stent Grafts
abstract: Abstract Background To compare short-term computed tomography angiography (CTA) findings after frozen elephant trunk (FET) for type A aortic dissection (TAAD) using a single-branched stent graft (Fontus) versus a straight stent graft (Cronus). Methods A single-center retrospective study (July 1, 2021 – August 31, 2024) included 189 TAAD patients (Fontus, n = 111; Cronus, n = 78) after excluding anatomical contraindications. Postoperative CTA assessed branch endoleak, stented-segment false lumen thrombosis, and distal stent-induced new entry (dSINE). Inverse probability of treatment weighting balanced baseline differences. Results Stented-segment false lumen thrombosis was comparable between Fontus and Cronus, indicating non-inferior performance of the branched design. In the Fontus cohort, branch-related endoleak occurred in 11 patients (10%) and was independently associated with left subclavian artery (LSA) involvement by dissection (odds ratio, 11.24; P = 0.003). Branch endoleak delayed complete thrombosis but did not alter mid-term remodeling. dSINE incidence did not differ by stent type but was independently driven by distal stent angulation (hazard ratio, 2.27 per 10°; P < 0.01); angles exceeding 30° were particularly hazardous. Conclusions Short-term CTA outcomes after FET for TAAD are comparable between Fontus and Cronus. Branch endoleak (10%) is the principal imaging limitation of the single-branched strategy and is predicted by LSA dissection involvement; thus, careful preoperative LSA assessment is advised. Across both stent types, distal angulation > 30° independently predicts dSINE, emphasizing the need for intraoperative geometric alignment and rigorous postoperative CTA surveillance.

title: Multi-Expert Measurement-Aware Learning for Carotid Intima-Media Complex Segmentation and Thickness Quantification in Ultrasound Images
abstract: Abstract Carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) is widely used as an ultrasound biomarker for evaluating vascular wall remodeling and early atherosclerotic changes. Reliable CIMT quantification requires accurate delineation of the far-wall intima-media complex (IMC), together with precise identification of the lumen-intima (LI) and media-adventitia (MA) interfaces. In clinical carotid B-mode ultrasound, however, IMC segmentation remains challenging because images are commonly degraded by speckle artifacts, weak contrast, and indistinct tissue boundaries. Moreover, annotations provided by different experts may vary in boundary placement, local thickness estimation, and labeled spatial extent, which can weaken the robustness of models trained under single-rater supervision. To reduce the influence of such annotation variability, this study develops a multi-expert measurement-aware learning framework for carotid IMC segmentation and IMT quantification. Based on the three expert annotations, A1, A1′, and A2, available in the technical version of the CUBS dataset, the proposed framework retains multi-expert supervisory information throughout training, enabling the model to learn more stable and representative IMC features. In addition, a measurement-aware loss is introduced to associate the LI and MA boundaries derived from the predicted mask with the resulting IMT error, thereby guiding the model toward both region-level segmentation accuracy and millimeter-scale thickness measurement precision. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves competitive IMC segmentation performance while producing a near-zero measurement bias of -0.0024 mm and strong absolute agreement with an ICC of 0.7268. These findings suggest that multi-expert measurement-aware learning offers an effective way to align IMC segmentation with the final IMT quantification target under multi-rater annotation variability, supporting more reliable automated carotid ultrasound measurement.

title: IT Band Syndrome Secondary to Osteogenic Cysts of the Proximal Tibia: A Rare Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Chronic localized pain over the proximal tibia is most often attributed to tendinopathy, degenerative disease, stress fracture, or benign bone lesions. Osteogenic cysts of the proximal tibia are rare and are usually considered as primary lesions in the differential diagnosis of a cortical lucency. It is far less recognized that such a cyst can act as a secondary trigger for chronic friction against the overlying iliotibial (IT) band, producing IT band syndrome as a consequence of the underlying bony pathology rather than as an independent process. We report a rare case in which IT band syndrome developed secondary to an osteogenic cyst of the proximal tibia. Case presentation A 45-year-old woman presented with several months of progressively worsening pain over the anterolateral aspect of the left proximal leg, aggravated by walking, prolonged standing, and stair climbing, without preceding trauma or constitutional symptoms. Examination revealed localized tenderness over the lateral proximal tibia, with pain on terminal knee movements. Plain radiographs showed a small, well-defined mixed lesion of the proximal tibia over lateral aspect, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated a well-circumscribed cortical lesion with surrounding marrow edema and reactive soft-tissue change. Surgical exploration confirmed an intraosseous osteogenic cyst measuring 2.2 × 1.5 cm, with an adjacent, secondarily thickened fibrous band arising from chronic irritation of the IT band by the underlying cyst. fluoroscopy guided assessment of the lesion confirmed cystic material with a bony, cement-like consistency, in keeping with an osteogenic cyst. Complete excision of the cystic contents and the reactive fibrous band was performed. Histopathology confirmed bony material within the lesion, together with dense fibrocollagenous tissue and fibroblastic proliferation in the adjacent band, consistent with cyst-driven IT band syndrome. The patient had complete resolution of symptoms without recurrence at follow-up. Conclusions An osteogenic cyst of the proximal tibia can be an underrecognized secondary cause of IT band syndrome through chronic frictional irritation of the overlying band. Awareness of this association supports earlier imaging-directed diagnosis, appropriate intraoperative exploration, and complete excision of both the cyst and the reactive soft-tissue changes, which together provide excellent clinical outcomes.

title: Upper Airway Morphology on Lateral Radiographs and Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation Outcome
abstract: Abstract Purpose Treatment response to hypoglossal nerve stimulation (HNS) for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) remains variable despite stringent selection criteria. We evaluated whether upper airway anatomy and electrode cuff position on postoperative lateral radiographs are associated with HNS treatment response. Methods Postoperative lateral radiographs were analyzed using standardized cephalometric measurements of the spatial relationships between the hyoid bone, mandible, cervical spine, and electrode cuff. The primary outcome was reduction in the apnea–hypopnea index (AHI). Secondary outcomes included associations between radiographic measurements, responder status according to the Sher criteria, and baseline characteristics. Results Fifty-three patients (23% female) with a median age of 62.4 years and median body mass index of 27.0 kg/m² were included. Median AHI decreased from 39.3 (interquartile range, IQR, 25.8–51.8) to 24.3 (IQR, 12.6–35.4) events/hour (P < .001). Among all measurements, only the angle between the hyoid bone and electrode cuff correlated with absolute AHI reduction (Spearman’s rho = 0.39, 95% CI 0.14–0.60; adjusted P = .029). Responders also exhibited a larger angle between the hyoid bone and electrode cuff, although this was not significant after adjustment for multiple testing (P = .042; adjusted P = .111). No other radiographic parameter was associated with treatment response. Conclusion HNS significantly improved objective and subjective outcomes; however, static upper airway anatomy and electrode cuff position on lateral radiographs showed limited value for predicting treatment response. These findings suggest that non-anatomical factors, including upper airway collapsibility and arousal threshold, may contribute more to HNS outcomes than static anatomy.

title: Impact of AI-assisted chest radiography on clinical decision-making: A temporal analysis of CT referral rates and the proportion of positive CT in cardiology outpatient setting
abstract: Abstract Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly integrated into chest radiography (CXR) interpretation to assist in the detection of pulmonary abnormalities. However, whether AI-assisted interpretation influences subsequent clinical decision-making in routine practice remains unclear. We investigated the association between the implementation of AI-assisted CXR interpretation and subsequent clinical decision-making, focusing on chest computed tomography (CT) referral and the detection of clinically relevant pulmonary abnormalities in a cardiology outpatient setting. Methods: We retrospectively identified adult patients who underwent CXR at their first visit to a cardiology outpatient department between March 2020 and February 2024. A commercially available AI system was routinely applied to CXR examinations throughout the study period. Patients were divided into two consecutive periods according to the date of CXR acquisition, and temporal trends were additionally evaluated by acquisition year. The primary outcome was referral for chest CT within 30 days after CXR, and the secondary outcome was the proportion of CT referrals resulting in positive findings. Generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) incorporating cardiologist-level random effects were used to evaluate temporal changes in CT referral and positive CT findings. originalAbstract:
Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly integrated into chest radiography (CXR) interpretation to assist in the detection of pulmonary abnormalities. However, whether AI-assisted interpretation influences subsequent clinical decision-making in routine practice remains unclear. We investigated the association between the implementation of AI-assisted CXR interpretation and subsequent clinical decision-making, focusing on chest computed tomography (CT) referral and the detection of clinically relevant pulmonary abnormalities in a cardiology outpatient setting.

Methods:

We retrospectively identified adult patients who underwent CXR at their first visit to a cardiology outpatient department between March 2020 and February 2024. A commercially available AI system was routinely applied to CXR examinations throughout the study period. Patients were divided into two consecutive periods according to the date of CXR acquisition, and temporal trends were additionally evaluated by acquisition year. The primary outcome was referral for chest CT within 30 days after CXR, and the secondary outcome was the proportion of CT referrals resulting in positive findings. Generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) incorporating cardiologist-level random effects were used to evaluate temporal changes in CT referral and positive CT findings.

Results:

A total of 9279 patients were included, comprising 5320 patients in the earlier period and 3959 in the later period. The CT referral rate was significantly higher in the later period than in the earlier period. In GLMM analysis, the likelihood of CT referral increased significantly over time (odds ratio [OR], 1.846; p  < 0.001). Year-to-year trend analysis demonstrated significant increases in both the overall CT referral rate (OR, 1.192; p  < 0.001) and the proportion of positive CT (OR, 1.335; p  < 0.001).

Conclusions:

Our research suggests that AI may help cardiologists' interpretation of CXR by facilitating the identification of unexpected pulmonary abnormalities and enhancing proper clinical decision-making and further diagnostic evaluation with continued use.

title: Chemotherapy-Refractory Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma with Concurrent Long-Segment Intramedullary Spinal Metastases and Brain Metastases:Case Reports and Literature Review
abstract: Abstract Background Intramedullary spinal metastases (ISCM) are an extremely rare complication of systemic malignant tumors affecting the central nervous system, with a very poor prognosis,Among these, esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is particularly rare as a primary tumor.To date, there have been only seven documented cases of ISCM associated with esophageal cancer,In all cases, involvement was limited to a single segment of the spinal cord.This article reports the first case of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) with long-segment intramedullary metastasis in the thoracic segment during chemotherapy, complicated by concurrent brain metastases. Case Presentation A 69-year-old male patient with advanced ESCC (cT4N1M1, with liver metastases),After receiving three cycles of albumin-bound paclitaxel combined with cisplatin chemotherapy,The patient presented with acute pain in the left shoulder and right lower limb, weakness in the right lower limb (Grade IV on the Medical Research Council muscle strength scale), and decreased sensation in the abdomen.Gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the spinal cord revealed extensive intramedullary lesions spanning long segments from T1 to T12,Accompanied by characteristic ring-shaped enhancement,accompanied by characteristic ring-shaped enhancement,at the same time, edema of the cervical spinal cord is visible, but there is no enhancement.A concurrent cranial MRI revealed one new annular enhancing nodule in the left frontal lobe and one in the right cerebellum.Given the widespread involvement of the central nervous system and the family’s refusal of surgery and radiation therapy, the patient died 15 days after discharge. Conclusion Even in patients in whom systemic chemotherapy appears to be effective, ISCM can still occur, possibly due to tumor cells crossing the blood-spinal cord barrier via the hematogenous route.Gadolinium-enhanced MRI and annular enhancement are key to the diagnosis.This case highlights that when acute neurological symptoms occur during cancer treatment, the threshold for ordering neuroimaging should be lowered,this allows for early detection, thereby giving some patients the opportunity to undergo palliative radiation therapy or surgery.

title: Evaluation of Bone Mineral Density in Type II Diabetic and Nondiabetic Individuals in a Mandibular Load-Bearing Region: A Pilot Study
abstract: Abstract Aim To evaluate and compare the Bone mineral density (BMD) of the mandibular first molar area in patients with type II diabetes mellitus (T2DM) compared with nondiabetic subjects by using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), and its possible use in pre-implant treatment planning. Materials and Methods A prospective cross-sectional pilot study was conducted in 32 subjects, including 16 with T2DM and 16 systemically healthy controls. CBCT scans were obtained using standardised imaging parameters. Assessment of bone density was done by measuring greyscale values (GVs) in three regions of interest within the mandibular first molar region. These include the crestal bone, 2mm apical to the crest and basal trabecular bone. The mean grey scale values for both groups were compared using appropriate statistical tests, with p < 0.05 considered significant. Glycaemic status will be assessed by measuring Glycated Haemoglobin (HbA1c) levels. Results The diabetic group demonstrated significantly lower mean BMD than the nondiabetic group across all assessed regions (p < 0.005). Age-wise distribution revealed a higher proportion of diabetic patients in the 55–65 years group (62.5%) than in the nondiabetic group (43.75%), indicating a significant association with advancing age (p < 0.005). Statistical analysis was conducted using descriptive and inferential statistics, particularly the chi-square test and Student’s unpaired t-test. The tools utilised in statistical analysis were SPSS 27.0 and GraphPad Prism 7.0. Significance level (p<0.05). Conclusion Type II diabetes mellitus is associated with reduced bone density in the mandibular first molar region, as assessed by grayscale values on cone-beam computed tomography. Site-specific evaluation of bone quality before implant placement may improve treatment planning and assist in recognising patients who require modified surgical protocols. Clinical Significance A comprehensive implant site assessment supports predictive treatment planning, enabling customised implant protocols that improve prosthetic stability. Ongoing monitoring of glycaemic impacts aids effective risk stratification and helps develop evidence-based guidelines.

title: Timing-Aware Delta-Radiomics After Microwave Ablation of Hepatocellular Carcinoma: An Exploratory MRI Study
abstract: Abstract Background Delta-radiomics may capture treatment-induced imaging changes after thermal ablation, but early post-ablation MRI appearance evolves with time. We explored whether restriction of the first post-ablation MRI to a standardized early follow-up window was associated with different discrimination of local tumor progression (LTP) after complete microwave ablation of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods This retrospective single-center lesion-level study included HCC lesions with initial complete ablation and MRI follow-up. Radiomics features were extracted from pre-ablation tumor and first post-ablation ablation-zone volumes of interest on arterial-phase contrast-enhanced T1-weighted VIBE MRI. Delta features were defined as post-ablation minus pre-ablation values. Time to LTP was evaluated using Kaplan–Meier and Cox models. Twelve-month discrimination was assessed using patient-level grouped cross-validation and patient-level bootstrap confidence intervals. Analyses across all post-ablation MRI timings characterized performance in the full evaluable cohort, and a prespecified 20–60-day post-ablation MRI window was examined as a timing-standardized sensitivity analysis. Results In 29 lesions from 28 patients, 12- and 24-month LTP-free survival rates were 0.708 and 0.629, respectively. Tumor size was associated with higher LTP risk. In the 12-month radiomics cohort (24 lesions, 7 events), the clinical model achieved an AUC of 0.731 (95% CI: 0.456–0.970), and adding radiomics across all timings did not improve discrimination. In the 20–60-day subset (21 lesions, 7 events), higher AUC point estimates were observed for pre-ablation plus delta-radiomics (0.888; 95% CI: 0.690–1.000) and clinical plus pre-ablation plus delta-radiomics (0.908; 95% CI: 0.731–1.000). The restricted subset differed from the all-timing cohort by only three lesions. Conclusions Post-ablation MRI timing may contribute to delta-radiomics variability after HCC microwave ablation. The higher 12-month AUC estimates observed in the 20–60-day subset are hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as evidence that this window is optimal or that the model is clinically validated. Larger multicenter cohorts with external validation are required.

title: Non-contrast CT Radiomics Combined with Clinical Features for Predicting Secondary Sepsis in Severe Acute Pancreatitis
abstract: Abstract Objective: To evaluate models based on non-contrast computed tomography (CT) radiomics and early clinical data for predicting secondary sepsis in patients with severe acute pancreatitis (SAP). Methods: This retrospective single-centre study included 253 patients with SAP admitted to the Second Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University between January 2021 and December 2025. Patients were allocated to a training cohort (n = 202) and an internal test cohort (n = 51) using an approximately 8:2 stratified random split. The first eligible non-contrast abdominal CT examination performed within 1 week of symptom onset was used to delineate the pancreas and contiguous peripancreatic inflammatory lesions. A total of 107 radiomics features were extracted using PyRadiomics. All candidate predictors were obtained before a prespecified prediction time point. Feature standardisation, selection and model development were conducted exclusively in the training cohort, and the training-derived classification thresholds were applied unchanged to the test cohort. Logistic regression was used to develop a clinical signature, a radiomics signature and a combined nomogram. Discrimination, calibration and clinical utility were assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, the Hosmer-Lemeshow test and decision curve analysis. Results: Secondary sepsis occurred in 54 patients in the training cohort and 14 in the test cohort. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression retained eight radiomics features. In the training cohort, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.858 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.806-0.909) for the clinical signature, 0.675 (95% CI, 0.587-0.762) for the radiomics signature and 0.867 (95% CI, 0.814-0.919) for the combined nomogram. In the test cohort, the corresponding AUCs were 0.699 (95% CI, 0.542-0.855), 0.697 (95% CI, 0.550-0.843) and 0.732 (95% CI, 0.593-0.870), respectively. The combined nomogram achieved a sensitivity of 0.929 and a negative predictive value of 0.955, whereas the clinical signature achieved a specificity of 0.757. The radiomics signature showed no evidence of lack of fit in either cohort (P = 0.508 and P = 0.306). Conclusions: A radiomics signature derived from non-contrast CT may provide complementary information for risk stratification of secondary sepsis in SAP. The combined nomogram showed the highest AUC and a high negative predictive value in the internal test cohort, but its performance and calibration require confirmation and recalibration in larger external multicentre cohorts.

title: Scalability of the Mechanobiological Vulnerability Index (MVI) in Triple- Negative Breast Cancer: A Microgravity-Induced Platform for In Silico Target Discovery
abstract: Abstract Triple-negative breast cancer remains one of modern oncology’s most critical challenges, characterized by the absence of hormone receptors and HER2 overexpression—a profile that drastically restricts targeted therapeutic options and is associated with high aggressiveness, increased metastatic risk, and unfavorable prognosis. Despite advances in genomics-based precision oncology, limitations persist regarding approaches that consider only static molecular profiles without accounting for the fundamental physical and mechanical properties of tumor cells. Here, we propose the Mechanobiological Vulnerability Index (MVI), a scalable computational platform conceived on mechanobiological principles to investigate the hypothesis that simulated microgravity conditions induce profound structural alterations in the cytoskeleton and cell adhesion complexes—a disorganization capable of exposing neoantigens and cryptic epitopes normally masked under terrestrial gravity. The methodological strategy integrates experimental models of gravitational simulation with advanced deep learning architectures: U-Net networks for segmentation and structural analysis, and Vision Transformers (ViT) to capture complex patterns of morphological deformation. The MVI calculation formula is theoretically established as a quantitative metric that synthesizes deformation magnitude, degree of structural disorganization, alterations in mechanical signaling pathways, and the level of exposure of biological targets. It is anticipated that this methodological framework, when implemented and validated in subsequent stages, will exhibit a high degree of transferability to different tumor types, constituting an innovative complementary tool for the discovery of novel therapeutic targets and for deepening the understanding of the relationships between the physical properties of tumor cells and their response to treatments.

title: IL-17+ lymphocytes mark low-immunity, EMT-enriched tumors in primary triple-negative breast cancer: investigated in relation to tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (CD8+, CD4+, FOXP3+) and macrophages (CD163+)
abstract: Abstract Background The immunological response in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is of clinical value. In this study, we investigated the prognostic relevance of distinct immune cell subpopulations in TNBC, their interrelationships and their associated molecular profiles. Material & methods IL-17+, CD8+, CD4+ and FOXP3+ lymphocytes and CD163+ macrophages were quantified by immunohistochemistry in tissue microarrays, while tumor infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) were assessed on H&E-stained slides in a population-based Swedish cohort of 237 patients with early-stage TNBC diagnosed 2010-2015. Chemotherapy (CT) was administered to 171 patients (155 adjuvant, 16 neoadjuvant). Analyses were conducted on CT-naive tumor tissue. Survival was evaluated using Cox proportional hazards regression and molecular profiling performed by analysing RNA-sequencing data. Results High CD8+, CD4+, FOXP3+ and stromal CD163+ were all positively correlated and associated with improved prognosis in CT-treated patients. In contrast, IL-17+ lymphocytes were inversely correlated with TILs and the other immune cell subsets and their prognostic impact was non-significant, although hazard ratios suggested a potential adverse prognostic effect for invasive disease-free survival. RNA-sequencing analysis demonstrated that tumors infiltrated with IL-17+ lymphocytes were characterized by enrichment of epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) and pathways associated with metabolic reprogramming and cellular stress adaptation, while immune/inflammatory- and cell cycle-related pathways showed weak or no enrichment. The enrichment pattern for IL-17+ tumors contrasted with those high in TILs and the other immune cell subpopulations. Conclusions This study demonstrates that primary TNBC tumors infiltrated by IL-17+ lymphocytes represent a distinct phenotype characterized by enrichment of EMT and reduced overall immune activity, with potential implications for patient stratification and therapeutic strategies. Trial Registration The Swedish Cancerome Analysis Network – Breast (SCAN-B) study was retrospectively registered 2 nd Dec 2014 at ClinicalTrials.gov; ID NCT02306096.

title: Mechanobiological Vulnerability Index (MVI) in Lung Cancer: A Computer Vision Protocol for Identifying Therapeutic Targets under Simulated Microgravity
abstract: Abstract Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains among the leading causes of cancer mortality worldwide, due to its high phenotypic plasticity, biomechanical adaptation, and resistance to available treatments. Although precision oncology has advanced significantly through the genomic and molecular characterization of tumors, current approaches still present limitations in capturing the dynamic mechanobiological alterations that influence tumor progression and therapeutic response. Considering that lung tissue is continually subjected to physiological cycles of expansion and retraction during respiration, NSCLC cells develop a cytoskeletal organization that is highly adaptive to the mechanical forces of the microenvironment. ​This study proposes the application of the Mechanobiological Vulnerability Index (MVI), a computational index previously developed for evaluating mechanobiological vulnerability in solid tumors, to quantify structural alterations in three-dimensional NSCLC spheroids subjected to simulated microgravity. The protocol integrates three-dimensional spheroid culture, rotating wall bioreactors (Rotating Cell Culture System – RCCS), and a hybrid computer vision pipeline combining U-Net-based semantic segmentation with Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures. Based on the temporal analysis of cellular deformations, parameters related to plasma membrane deformation, cytoskeletal organization, mechanotransduction, and the exposure of cryptic epitopes are estimated and subsequently integrated into the MVI calculation. ​The central hypothesis of the work is that simulated microgravity induces a progressive perturbation of the biomechanical stability of tumor spheroids, producing a transient window of greater structural vulnerability that can be quantified by the MVI. The identification of this transition could contribute to the future development of mechanobiological biomarkers capable of assisting in the temporal optimization of therapeutic interventions. ​Instead of proposing a definitive therapeutic strategy, this work presents a methodological protocol that integrates mechanobiology, artificial intelligence, and computer vision to investigate the biomechanical adaptation of lung tumors under simulated microgravity conditions. It is expected that this approach will establish a reproducible platform for future experimental studies and contribute to the development of strategies based on the physical properties of the tumor microenvironment in precision oncology.

title: Semi-Automated Quantitative CT–Enhanced GAP Index for Prognostic Assessment in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
abstract: Abstract Background Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is marked by spatially heterogeneous fibrotic remodeling and highly variable clinical trajectories, which limit the precision of existing prognostic tools. Widely used indices, such as GAP (Gender–Age–Physiology), rely on physiological measurements and do not explicitly capture anatomical disease burden. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI)–assisted 3D quantitative Computed Tomography (CT) imaging enable objective, volumetric characterization of lung fibrosis and provide a foundation for radiology-integrated prognostic modeling. Methods We developed and evaluated an AI-assisted quantitative CT framework for prognostic assessment in patients with IPF. Whole-lung segmentation was performed using a pretrained deep learning model (LungMask), followed by semi-automated segmentation of fibrotic abnormalities with radiologist-guided refinement. Quantitative imaging biomarkers, including honeycombing volume, non-honeycomb fibrotic lung volume, preserved lung volume, and the pathological lung volume-to-total lung volume ratio, were derived from 3D CT analysis. This radiological parameter was integrated into the conventional GAP index to create a radiology-enhanced prognostic model. Prognostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and Kaplan–Meier survival analysis. Results A total of 116 patients with IPF were included in the study (mean age: 64.2 ± 9.2 years; 69.8% male). During a median follow-up of 40.5 months, 44% of patients died. Patients who died had significantly lower baseline pulmonary function parameters and greater fibrotic lung involvement on AI-assisted quantitative CT analysis than survivors (all p < 0.05). The pathological lung volume-to-total lung volume ratio showed good prognostic performance for predicting mortality (AUC = 0.795, 95% CI: 0.713–0.877, p < 0.001). Integrating this radiological parameter into the conventional GAP index further improved prognostic performance (AUC = 0.805, 95% CI: 0.725–0.885, p < 0.001) compared with the GAP index alone (AUC = 0.712, 95% CI: 0.618–0.807). Kaplan–Meier analysis showed significant survival differences among modified GAP risk groups, with median survival of 100 months for patients with a score ≤ 6 and 48 months for those with a score ≥ 7 (log-rank p < 0.001). Conclusions This study presents an interpretable, AI-assisted quantitative CT imaging framework that integrates objective measures of fibrotic lung burden into an established clinical prognostic index. By unifying volumetric CT biomarkers with physiological scoring, the proposed model improves prognostic precision while maintaining clinical usability. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI)–assisted 3D quantitative Computed Tomography (CT) imaging enable objective, volumetric characterization of lung fibrosis and provide a foundation for radiology-integrated prognostic modeling. Methods We developed and evaluated an AI-assisted quantitative CT framework for prognostic assessment in patients with IPF. Whole-lung segmentation was performed using a pretrained deep learning model (LungMask), followed by semi-automated segmentation of fibrotic abnormalities with radiologist-guided refinement. Quantitative imaging biomarkers, including honeycombing volume, non-honeycomb fibrotic lung volume, preserved lung volume, and the pathological lung volume-to-total lung volume ratio, were derived from 3D CT analysis. This radiological parameter was integrated into the conventional GAP index to create a radiology-enhanced prognostic model. Prognostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and Kaplan–Meier survival analysis. By unifying volumetric CT biomarkers with physiological scoring, the proposed model improves prognostic precision while maintaining clinical usability. This work highlights the potential of AI-assisted quantitative imaging as a scalable, translational tool for personalized risk stratification in fibrotic lung disease.

title: The Changing Burden of Multiple Sclerosis in Bahrain, 2013–2026: Foundational Epidemiology, Contemporary Registry-Based Case Ascertainment, and Genetic Insights in a Changing Arabian Gulf MS Landscape
abstract: Abstract Background Bahrain’s 2011–2013 multiple sclerosis (MS) registry established the country’s first epidemiological baseline using the 2010 McDonald criteria. Since then, diagnostic criteria, MRI access, specialist care, and follow-up have evolved, while Bahrain and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) studies suggest HLA and non-HLA susceptibility signals. The present analysis links the foundational baseline to March 2026 registry-based case ascertainment and a one-year new-diagnosis count, allowing contemporary prevalence and incidence to be considered together while preserving the distinction between registry ascertainment and a formal population survey. Objective To compare the 2013 and 2026 clinically recognized MS burden among Bahraini citizens, quantify contemporary crude registry-based prevalence and incidence, and contextualize the findings with emerging Bahraini and GCC genetic and environmental evidence. Materials and Methods This retrospective registry-based descriptive analysis included 287 Bahraini patients fulfilling the 2010 McDonald criteria and identified through Salmaniya Medical Complex between 1 July 2011 and 31 October 2013. The March 2026 count combined Salmaniya Medical Complex and National Bank of Bahrain Multiple Sclerosis Centre records. Crude prevalence was estimated from 876 actively followed patients using a Bahraini-citizen denominator of 747,500, with sensitivity analysis across 745,000–755,000. From March 2025 to March 2026, 48 newly diagnosed Bahraini patients were registered; crude registry-based incidence and an exact Poisson 95% confidence interval (CI) were calculated. Only aggregate data were analyzed. Contemporary GCC epidemiology and relevant diagnostic, environmental, genetic, and treatment evidence were reviewed narratively. Results The foundational cohort had a female-to-male ratio of 2.49:1, mean age at onset of 35 ± 10.2 years, median Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 2.0, reported prevalence of 59.9 per 100,000 Bahraini citizens (recalculated 95% CI, 53.0–66.8), and annual incidence of 5.8 per 100,000 (95% CI, 2.8–8.87) during 2012–2013. By March 2026, 876 patients were actively followed, 589 more than the foundational count and 3.05-fold that count. Estimated crude registry-based prevalence was 117.2 per 100,000 (95% CI, 109.4–125.0; sensitivity range, 116.0–117.6). The 48 newly diagnosed patients yielded a crude registry-based incidence of 6.4 per 100,000 (95% CI, 4.7–8.5). Conclusion Bahrain’s clinically recognized MS burden has increased substantially, while the contemporary one-year incidence estimate remains broadly similar to the earlier estimate. This pattern is compatible with a combination of epidemiological change, cumulative prevalence, improved ascertainment, diagnostic sensitivity, survival, and specialist follow-up rather than a proportional rise in annual new diagnoses. Differences in diagnostic eras and ascertainment preclude direct causal attribution. Prospective national registration integrating clinical, imaging, treatment, environmental, and genetic data is needed to define the evolving burden and its determinants.

title: Distance mapping analysis of tibiotalar joint in varus ankle osteoarthritis using 3D bone reconstruction of weight-bearing CT scans
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Varus ankle osteoarthritis (OA) is a common condition in which malalignment-related eccentric loading leads to progressive medial joint degeneration. Surgical treatment decision depends on the extent and distribution of joint space narrowing. Weight-bearing computed tomography (WBCT) combined with three-dimensional (3D) bone reconstruction software now enables distance mapping analysis, which can quantify regional tibiotalar joint space more precisely than conventional radiography. The purpose of this study was to visualize and quantify regional joint space narrowing patterns of the tibiotalar joint across stages of varus ankle OA using an auto-segmentation technique and distance mapping analysis applied to WBCT images. Methods In this retrospective study, WBCT scans of 60 ankles from 36 patients were obtained and classified according to the modified Takakura classification into three groups: control (stage 0–1; n = 29), moderate OA (stages 2 and 3a; n = 19), grouped based on joint space narrowing confined to the medial gutter, and severe OA (stages 3b and 4; n = 12), defined by obliteration extending to the talar dome. All WBCT images were analyzed using 3D auto-segmentation and distance mapping software (Bonelogic® Ortho Foot and Ankle, Disior, Finland). The talar articular surface was divided into eight regions of interest (two medial gutter and six talar dome sub-regions), and the joint space distance was measured as the shortest surface-to-surface distance from each point on the talus to the adjacent tibial plafond. Results Compared with controls, the moderate OA group showed significantly reduced distances at the anterior medial gutter (MMA: 2.14 ± 0.06 vs. 1.76 ± 0.11 mm, p = 0.033), the anteromedial talar dome (TMA: 2.71 ± 0.10 vs. 2.35 ± 0.11 mm, p < 0.001), and the central posterior dome (TCP: 2.54 ± 0.06 vs. 2.42 ± 0.14 mm, p < 0.001). In the severe OA group, further reductions were observed across medial and central dome regions, with the most pronounced narrowing at the anteromedial dome (TMA: 1.34 ± 0.15 mm, p < 0.001 vs. controls), and significant decreases at the posteromedial dome, and both anterior and posterior central dome (all p < 0.01 vs. controls). No significant changes were detected at the lateral talar dome (TLA, TLP) across any group comparison. Conclusion WBCT-based distance mapping revealed that joint space narrowing in varus ankle OA follows a characteristic spatial pattern: moderate disease predominantly affects the anterior medial gutter and anteromedial dome, while severe disease extends across medial and central dome regions with consistent lateral preservation. These findings provide 3D quantitative support for the clinical importance of talar dome involvement in severity grading. In preoperative planning for realignment osteotomy, distance mapping may help identify the regions of degenerative cartilage loss and guide load redistribution toward preserved areas, particularly the lateral talar dome and posterior medial gutter.

title: AI-Based Approaches for the Identification and Quantification of Traumatic Brain Injury in Computed Tomography Imaging: Systematic Review.
abstract: Background Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of global disability and mortality, requiring timely diagnosis to prevent secondary injury. Manual computed tomographic (CT) evaluation often causes diagnostic delays, especially in smaller hospitals with limited radiological expertise. AI methods have been increasingly proposed to automate CT-based TBI assessment. objectives The aim of this review is to present a comprehensive review of AI techniques applied to CT scans for TBI assessment. Methods This study presents a systematized review conducted in accordance with PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 reporting guidelines. Titles, abstracts, and full texts were screened against predefined eligibility criteria. Data on datasets, model architectures, preprocessing, and performance metrics were extracted using a structured form. Risk of bias was not formally assessed using a standardized tool. Instead, we qualitatively evaluated common sources of bias, such as dataset size, clinical evaluation, and external validation. Due to substantial heterogeneity in tasks, datasets, and outcome measures, we performed narrative synthesis only. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore from inception to December 31, 2025, for English-language peer-reviewed studies. We included original research papers that used AI or machine learning methods applied to human noncontrast head CT for TBI-related assessment. Studies had to report quantitative performance metrics. Nonoriginal papers, non-CT modalities, pediatric-only cohorts, and non-TBI applications were excluded. We restricted inclusion to English-language, peer-reviewed studies and did not perform a formal risk-of-bias or publication-bias assessment, which may overestimate the strength of the evidence. Results By screening the 674 publications found, we identified 101 studies for evaluation. We grouped these 101 studies into 4 categories: binary TBI classification (TBI or non-TBI), hemorrhage detection (classification, localization, segmentation, and quantization), midline shift measurement, and increased intracranial pressure estimation. Most work focused on hemorrhage detection, with fewer studies on TBI severity classification, midline shift estimation, and increased intracranial pressure assessment. Reported performance was frequently high, but many studies relied on small, single-center datasets, limited annotation detail, and internal validation only. External validation and prospective clinical evaluation were rare. Conclusions AI methods for CT-based TBI assessment demonstrate strong performance in retrospective evaluations under controlled conditions, particularly for hemorrhage detection and segmentation; however, the current evidence base is constrained by limited dataset diversity, incomplete reporting, and lack of clinical validation. Accordingly, these findings should be interpreted as evidence of methodological feasibility rather than clinical readiness.

title: Tumor-Intrinsic Blood and Imaging Correlatives in Advanced Prostate Cancer Treated with Combination Radiopharmaceutical Therapy and Immunotherapy.
abstract: The PRINCE trial showed the clinical activity for 177 Lu-PSMA-617 in combination with pembrolizumab for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. To refine patient selection and improve response monitoring strategies to this combination, we investigated candidate tumor-intrinsic biomarkers of treatment response and resistance. Methods: We performed circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), circulating tumor cell (CTC), and PET imaging analyses at baseline, 12 wk on-treatment, and disease progression in participants enrolled in PRINCE ( n = 37). We performed targeted sequencing for ctDNA quantification and genomic analysis of more than 70 prostate cancer genes. CTC enumeration was performed on the EpicSciences platform and was combined with selective single-cell whole-genome sequencing. PET imaging included serial PSMA PET as well as 18 F-FDG PET imaging at baseline. Results: A low baseline ctDNA fraction and high PSMA avidity in metastatic lesions were linked to superior treatment responses and may have composite biomarker value. Genomic alterations in tumor suppressor genes TP53, RB1, or PTEN were associated with higher 18 F-FDG avidity and metabolic tumor volume on 18 F-FDG PET imaging and worse prognosis. At 12-wk on-treatment, both ctDNA detection and PSMA PET imaging were strong indicators of response depth and durability. At disease progression, PSMA expression on PET imaging was lower compared with baseline and supported by subclonal remodeling of ctDNA and CTC copy number profiles and by clonal expansions of tumor suppressor gene mutations. Conclusion: We provide the first integrated molecular and imaging insights into determinants of response and resistance to combined radiopharmaceutical therapy and immunotherapy in prostate cancer and propose biomarker strategies to inform future clinical development.

title: Bibliometric and Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) analysis of artificial intelligence for thyroid nodules.
abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly integrated into thyroid nodule ultrasound diagnosis and malignant risk stratification, fostering a fast-growing interdisciplinary domain encompassing endocrinology, medical imaging, and computational intelligence. Nevertheless, existing bibliometric studies in this field rely on single-database datasets and short time-series windows, lacking systematic elaboration of the dynamic linkage between clinical guideline iterations and AI algorithm evolution. This study conducted a comprehensive bibliometric analysis to fill this research gap, clarify the global intellectual landscape, and reveal the evolutionary rules and emerging frontiers of AI-assisted thyroid nodule diagnosis. Methods Peer-reviewed articles and reviews on AI in thyroid nodule diagnosis were retrieved from Web of Science and PubMed (2006-2025). After strict data cleaning, 821 valid publications were analyzed using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and online platforms, examining publication trends, contributions, collaboration networks, citations, and keyword evolution. Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) was applied for topic modeling. Results The field showed rapid and sustained growth, with a compound annual growth rate of 24.1%, and a notable acceleration around 2017. In total, 2,870 authors from 75 countries contributed. China led global output, while the United States and South Korea showed higher citation quality. Shanghai Jiao Tong University was the most productive institution. Keyword analysis revealed close coupling with clinical guidelines (ATA, TI-RADS, Bethesda). Core hotspots included ultrasound image analysis, deep learning optimization, and malignant risk stratification. Emerging frontiers involve explainable AI, multimodal data fusion, and standardized clinical validation. Conclusions This study establishes a long-time-series, multi-database knowledge map of AI applications in thyroid nodule diagnosis, systematically revealing the global research pattern, spatiotemporal evolution characteristics, and guideline-driven developmental logic of this field. Different from previous single-dimensional bibliometric summaries, this work clarifies how standardized clinical diagnostic criteria chronologically correspond with the iterative progress of radiomics and deep learning research. The findings provide reliable theoretical references for subsequent algorithm optimization, interdisciplinary innovation, and large-scale multicenter prospective validation, facilitating the standardized clinical translation and high-quality development of AI-assisted thyroid diagnostic models and precision endocrinology.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven diabetic retinopathy research: mapping the evolution, coupling, and global collaboration landscape (1996-2026).
abstract: Background Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a major global cause of blindness. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has markedly impacted fundus screening over the past three decades, yet systematic bibliometric mapping of the knowledge architecture, evolutionary paths, and synergy among AI models, data modalities, and DR remains scarce. Objective This study conducted a comprehensive bibliometric analysis to characterize the AI-driven DR knowledge structure, collaboration networks, and hotspot migration, and to elucidate co-evolutionary dynamics among AI advances, data modality development, and DR research. Methods Following a systematic search and screening process, 12,741 publications were identified from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC), PubMed, and Scopus, spanning from January 1996 to June 2026. The analytical framework combined multiple methodologies: VOSviewer for collaborative network visualization, CiteSpace for burst detection and timeline mapping, and a Python-based text-mining pipeline for standardized extraction and normalization of AI model names, data modalities, and disease entities. Results The field exhibits a distinct three-stage evolutionary trajectory: the traditional machine learning era (1996-2014), the deep learning surge (2015-2019), and the current phase marked by the growing prominence of Transformer-based models (2020-present). The collaboration landscape is multipolar, with the United States, China, and India as hubs, while Singapore produces high-impact research. The knowledge base rests on algorithmic innovation and clinical validation. Convolutional neural networks have long served as the backbone architecture in the literature, while Vision Transformers have shown a clear upward trend in publication volume in recent years. Research hotspots are expanding from single-disease classification toward multimodal integration. Although fundus imaging remains the predominant data source, the potential of electronic health record narratives and multi-omics data is increasingly recognized. Overall, the research focus is shifting from "black-box" pattern recognition toward explainable AI and end-to-end clinical translation. Conclusion This study presents a systematic bibliometric mapping of AI-driven DR research, revealing high-frequency co-occurrence patterns between architectural specialization and clinical demands. Challenges persist in data integration, rare-disease evidence, and cross-setting validation. The future is likely to be shaped by multimodal foundation models and portable acquisition, transitioning AI toward comprehensive clinical decision support.

title: Optimizing systematic reviews in health sciences education: a mentefact-based algorithmic framework.
abstract: Introduction Systematic reviews in health sciences education require methodological approaches that address the pedagogical and conceptual complexity of educational interventions, which often differ from conventional clinical review models. This study addresses the research question: How can a mentefact-based algorithmic framework improve the rigor, consistency, and conceptual alignment of systematic reviews in health sciences education? Methodology The proposed framework comprises three linked modules: domain modeling through a mentefact, computational prioritization through rule-based filtering, semantic embeddings and clustering, and human-verified extraction and synthesis. The framework integrates the Ordinal Research Domain (ORD) and Conceptual Density and Experience Index (C-DEX) metrics to support source prioritization and conceptual relevance assessment. The workflow was structured with reference to PRISMA 2020 principles of transparency and reproducibility; however, the article reports a methodological framework with a pilot application, not a complete PRISMA-compliant systematic review. Results The framework was piloted in the topic of artificial intelligence in radiology education, a domain in which clinical, technical, and pedagogical terminologies frequently overlap. The pilot application showed that mentefact-guided filtering can improve conceptual alignment between the educational phenomenon under review and the screening strategy used to organize the evidence. Discussion Incorporating conceptual and pedagogical logic, rather than relying only on lexical keyword matching, may improve the interpretive relevance of evidence synthesis in health sciences education. Conclusion The framework is presented as a methodological proposal with a pilot application. Its performance requires validation in future studies using independent datasets, full reviewer-based reference standards, and formal metrics such as sensitivity, specificity, precision, recall, and inter-rater agreement.

title: Automated postoperative SLO quantification across clinically recorded cataract subtype groups: an exploratory cross-sectional study.
abstract: Objective To explore the application of automated quantitative scanning laser ophthalmoscopy analysis to early postoperative images and to characterize group-level variation in the resulting measurements across patients grouped according to clinically recorded age-related cataract subtype. Methods This retrospective observational imaging study included 716 eyes from 571 patients with age-related cataract who underwent phacoemulsification combined with intraocular lens implantation between August 2023 and August 2025. Early postoperative scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (SLO) images were analyzed using EVisionAI version 4.0 as a standardized automated quantitative image-analysis tool. Eyes were grouped as nuclear cataract (394 eyes), cortical cataract (217 eyes), or posterior subcapsular cataract (PSC; 105 eyes) according to routine preoperative slit-lamp records. Standardized LOCS III grading and cohort-specific validation of EVisionAI against manual annotations were not available in this retrospective dataset. Automated image-derived parameters included tessellated fundus-related features, optic disc morphology, peripapillary atrophy (PPA)-related parameters, and retinal vascular parameters. Patient-level baseline characteristics were compared using conventional statistical tests, as appropriate. Eye-level comparisons of automated image-derived SLO parameters were performed using generalized estimating equations to account for inter-eye correlation, with Wald χ 2 statistics reported. Multiple comparisons were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate procedure. Multivariable GEE models adjusted for age, sex, axial length, and cataract subtype were used to evaluate associations with selected imaging parameters. Standardized effect-size, age-overlap, and single-eye sensitivity analyses were also performed. Results After false discovery rate correction, multiple automated image-derived fundus parameters differed significantly among the retrospectively defined cataract subtype groups, including cup-to-disc ratio parameters, optic disc morphology, PPA-related parameters, and retinal vascular parameters. Compared with PSC eyes, nuclear and cortical cataract eyes showed relatively higher cup-to-disc ratio-related parameters and larger PPA-related parameters, whereas PSC eyes showed relatively greater retinal vessel length. Across age groups, tessellated fundus density, macular tessellated fundus density, optic disc-related tessellated fundus parameters, and PPA-related parameters increased significantly with age. Among the 14 contrasts involving the seven principal outcomes, standardized effect estimates were small to moderate (absolute standardized β, 0.258-0.619), and none met the descriptive threshold for a large effect. In multivariable GEE models, age remained associated with multiple tessellated fundus- and PPA-related parameters after adjustment for sex, axial length, and cataract subtype. Axial length also remained associated with optic disc tilt angle, PPA-related parameters, and tessellated fundus parameters. The age-overlap and single-eye sensitivity analyses showed generally consistent directions for the principal associations, although one optic disc tilt-angle contrast was attenuated after age restriction. Conclusion Automated quantitative SLO analysis was completed in 716 of 821 initially available early postoperative images. Group-level differences were observed across clinically recorded cataract subtype groups, but these findings were exploratory and may reflect non-standardized subtype assignment, unmeasured spherical-equivalent refractive error, age, axial length, image characteristics, and other confounding. They should not be interpreted as subtype-specific structural phenotypes or as evidence of diagnostic, prognostic, or clinical decision utility. Prospective studies with standardized cataract grading and cohort-specific algorithm validation are required.

title: Interpretable lung-constrained RegNetY-ViT framework for pulmonary tuberculosis classification in chest X-rays with radiological feature-guided neuro-symbolic reasoning.
abstract: Introduction Tuberculosis (TB) remains difficult to diagnose from chest X-rays due to overlapping radiological patterns with pneumonia, fibrotic scars, and other chronic lung abnormalities. Manual interpretation is highly dependent on expert experience and is often time-consuming, subjective, and prone to variability, especially in cases involving subtle or mixed lesion presentations. Methods This study proposes a RegNetY-ViT hybrid framework for chest X-ray analysis using the TBX11K dataset. RegNetY captures fine-grained local spatial features such as cavitary margins, consolidation, and fibronodular patterns, while ViT models global contextual relationships across the lung fields. Interpretability is embedded within the pipeline through multi-lesion Grad-CAM, enabling the localization of multiple abnormal regions. These attention maps are further refined into lesion masks using lung-constrained segmentation with adaptive thresholding, active contour refinement, and overlap validation. Radiological biomarkers, including upper-lobe infiltrates, cavitary changes, heterogeneous consolidation, and fibrotic distortion, are extracted and fed into a neuro-symbolic fuzzy inference system to translate imaging features into rule-based diagnostic support. Results The proposed hybrid model outperformed the standalone RegNetY and ViT models, particularly in detecting Active TB. It achieved an overall accuracy of 95.8%, macro-average sensitivity of 85.1%, macro-average specificity of 98.6%, and macro-average AUC of 87.2%. Interpretability analysis showed that Grad-CAM effectively localized disease-relevant lung regions, segmentation produced high consistency across lesion areas, and the neuro-symbolic layer generated clinically interpretable diagnostic explanations aligned with radiological biomarkers. Discussion The proposed RegNetY-ViT hybrid framework improves TB classification performance while enhancing interpretability through lesion localization and neuro-symbolic reasoning, thereby supporting more transparent and clinically meaningful decision-making in chest X-ray analysis.

title: Advances in MRI of glymphatic system dysfunction associated with obstructive sleep apnea and enlarged perivascular spaces.
abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is closely associated with an increased risk of cerebral small-vessel disease and cognitive impairment. OSA not only impairs cognitive function but also promotes the occurrence and development of enlarged perivascular spaces (EPVS) by impairing glymphatic system (GS) function. Perivascular spaces (PVS) are an important imaging marker of cerebral small-vessel disease and a morphological indicator of the functional status of the GS. However, the pathogenesis of OSA-related EPVS remains unclear, with GS dysfunction considered to be at its core. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a key tool for evaluating the association between OSA and EPVS, and emerging MRI techniques have provided imaging evidence to reveal the potential link between OSA-related GS dysfunction and EPVS formation. This article reviews the relationship between OSA severity, sleep structure, and the distribution of EPVS and focuses on the application of structural MRI, voxel-based morphometry, diffusion tensor imaging, diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular spaces, diffusion kurtosis imaging, dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI, phase-contrast and 4D flow MRI, and blood oxygen level-dependent functional MRI in the study of the relationship between OSA and EPVS.
